data.cultural_impact: The name Kuntal, derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kuntala’, meaning ‘coiled or twisted’, has been present in Hindu culture for centuries. It is believed to symbolize various aspects of traditional Indian art, pottery, and textiles - such as the intricate twists found in 'Kundalini' designs or the twisted coils of snakes used in Hindu iconography.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, the name Kuntal carries intense spiritual significance, particularly connected to Lord Shiva, the God of destruction and regeneration. The term ‘kuntala’ symbolizes Lord Shiva's power and protection, represented by his coiled snake, ‘Vasuki’, around his neck, which he uses both to destroy and create new life. Thus, the name Kuntal can be seen as a reminder of the strength and resilience one can gain through the power of the divine.

historical_references.reference: According to the Mahabharata, Kunti was a princess of Hastinapura and the elder sister of the Pandava brothers. She was impregnated by the god Indra, who appeared to her in the disguise of a snake. Kunti gave birth to Bhishma, Vidura, and three other sons, Yudhishthira, Bhima, and Arjuna.

The name Kuntal is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kuntala', which means 'dark-complexioned', 'tawny', or 'brindled'. This name is mentioned in the Rigveda, an ancient Indian text, and is believed to have been used to describe the horses or chariots of the gods.

The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'kuntala', meaning 'tangle-free'. It represents the pure and undisturbed flow of awareness towards the ultimate truth.
